title: Neyphug Thor bu gTor ma rgya rtsa'i phyag len sogs
shelf_note: A Neyphug Monastery manuscript bundle (BL). Its main text is Ngagchang Kunga Rinchen's Sakya practice of the hundred torma offerings, which belongs in this monastery collection.
structure_note: Each page record is one photograph of 3 pecha leaves (I5), so the reader sees three folios per 'page'. The bundle holds the same torma text twice: p1 leaves 2–3 (title page 'dpal sa skya pa sngags 'chang … gtor ma brgya rtsa'i phyag len') and p22 leaves 1–2 (a second copy beginning 'oM swa sti … gtor ma brgya rtsa gtong tshul') carry the same ritual wording. That fits a 'sogs' bundle and is not a duplicate scan, but the catalogue should say it. pages_ocr field 23 vs 35 pages that have OCR; 21/35 translated.

book_verdict: A Neyphug manuscript of a Sakya torma practice. The transcription is careful on running text, but the title page carries an OCR repetition loop: four invented lines of 'May merit be obtained!', which the translation renders.
reader_summary: A Sakya liturgy for offering the hundred tormas, by Ngagchang Kunga Rinchen, in a Neyphug bundle that has the text twice. Apart from the title page, the transcription matches the leaves line for line, and the English follows the Tibetan closely enough to perform the rite. The title page shows an invented block of repeated 'merit' lines, and a few names (Nanda/Upananda) are wrong.

title: Neyphug Thor bu Tshe khrid sogs
shelf_note: A Neyphug bundle of Nyingma empowerment manuals ('chi med dpal ster long-life, the Twelve Tenma, Rahula, Four-Armed Mahakala). It is a monastery collection and fits.
structure_note: Each page record is a photograph of 3 leaves (I5), and p57 is a single colophon leaf. The leaves in one photo can come from different texts in the bundle: on p5 the left-margin sigla differ and leaf 3 opens a new section, so 'page' order is not text order. The left- and right-margin folio numbers are not transcribed. 40/72 translated.

book_verdict: A sound Nyingma ritual bundle. The OCR matches the leaves line for line, and the translations are usable, with invented Markdown headings at the leaf breaks and some deity names calqued.
reader_summary: Empowerment and sadhana manuals from Neyphug: the long-life rite 'Bestowing the Splendor of Deathlessness', the Twelve Tenma life-entrustment, Rahula, and Four-Armed Mahakala. The transcription is of the right leaves, and the English follows it well enough for ritual study. Warn the reader that headings like '# Glorious Sonam Chokden!' are not in the source, and that some retinue names are calqued.

title: Neyphug Thor bu Pad gling bka' 'bum
shelf_note: Writings of Pema Lingpa (visions, supplications, songs, aspiration prayers), held at Neyphug. The work fits.
structure_note: Each page record is a photograph of 3 xylograph/manuscript leaves (I5). The pages_ocr field (153) disagrees with the 197 pages that have OCR; 146/197 translated. On p190 the abbreviation crosses on the leaf are transcribed as ྾, which is faithful.

book_verdict: Pema Lingpa's own writings, transcribed well. The English reads fluently, but it slips on hand gestures, speakers and names in ways a Bhutanese-Nyingma reader would catch.
reader_summary: Pema Lingpa's collected writings: visionary narratives, supplications to Longchenpa, an alphabet acrostic on Mahamudra-style view, and aspiration prayers. The Tibetan is the right text and largely accurate. The English is a usable reading aid, but not citable without checking: it gets a finger wrong, reverses a speaker, invents one lineage name, and in one prayer asks to abandon the ten virtues.

title: Neyphug Thor bu Phyag chen chos skor
shelf_note: A cycle of Kagyu/Shangpa-style Mahamudra instructions in dbu med, from Neyphug. Fits.
structure_note: Each page record is a photograph of 4 dbu med leaves (I5). Only 56 of 188 pages are translated, and the pages_ocr field (61) disagrees with the 188 pages that have OCR. The dbu med contractions (སེཾས, ཐཾད, ཡྔག) are kept as written, which is faithful, but they trip the translator (see p183).

tr_errors.problem: Saraha's line ('do not meditate with the mind; take all movement as meditation') becomes 'all beings shall meditate'

tr_errors.problem: 'Dakpo' added; the source says Kagyu

ocr_errors.problem: head mark transcribed with a different glyph

tr_errors.problem: ཡྔག is the dbu med contraction of yang dag ('look truly at the true; seeing the true, one is liberated', Ratnagotravibhāga), and the book's own p137 renders it so; here it becomes an invented simile about a yak

other.note: 'like a yak looking at itself' in a Mahamudra pith instruction reads as a howler

book_verdict: A rich dbu med Mahamudra cycle with accurate OCR. The English is mostly sound but does not consistently resolve dbu med contractions: one classic verse becomes 'a yak looking at itself'.
reader_summary: Kagyu Mahamudra instructions and songs (Lingrepa, Saraha, a stage-by-stage 'innate' guide), copied in cursive dbu med. The transcription is of the right leaves and keeps the scribe's contractions. Most of the English can be trusted for the sense, but it mistranslates at least one canonical verse and one Saraha line, and only about a third of the book is translated.
